title: Repair intermittent tenant-level metric blackout and sampled-span attribution during peak ingest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported dashboards showing complete tenant metric blackouts during short high-ingest spikes, coinciding with reduced sampled-span counts in trace explorer. Symptoms: (1) Timeseries tiles display series 'no data' for 30-90s windows, (2) Live traces for affected tenants show sampled spans missing or attributed to 'unknown-tenant', and (3) Alert channels did not fire because metric ingestion appeared to succeed at the shard level. This ticket coordinates diagnosis, hotfix, and rollout for Dedicated and Hosted control planes, plus a follow-up upgrade for Private deployments.
impact_summary: Three enterprise customers (dedicated) and several hosted tenants experienced missing dashboard tiles and incomplete trace contexts during peak traffic periods over 2026-03-09 to 2026-03-10. Customer-reported impact: degraded incident response and visibility; at least one customer escalated to SEV2 with business-critical monitoring blindspots. Estimated affected tenant-seconds: ~18k; user-facing product functionality unaffected but operational observability was degraded.
root_cause: Preliminary RCA points to two simultaneous failures: (A) a race in the metric window-rotation code in metrics-aggregator where metric shards momentarily moved to a pending state while coordinator updated shard-owner metadata; during this gap the ingestion pipeline wrote metrics to ephemeral tombstone buckets that the dashboard query path filters out, causing 'no data'. (B) a sampling-attribution mismatch: the trace sampler in the edge proxy uses a legacy tenant-id key 'x-tenant' while the collector normalizer expects 'tenant-id', leading to sampled spans being accepted but attribute-free and later classified as 'unknown-tenant' by the trace storage attribution step. The two issues correlate under high concurrency and shard rebalances.
reproduction_steps: 1) Simulate high concurrent ingest (1000s req/s) for a single tenant to trigger metric shard rebalance using internal load generator (run: tools/ingest-stress --tenant t-123 --rps 5k)
2) Observe metrics-aggregator logs for 'shard->pending' events; query dashboard tiles across 10s windows to see transient 'no data' gaps
3) At same time, send traced requests with mixed header keys (x-tenant and tenant-id) and sample at p=0.01; inspect collector normalized spans and verify 'tenant' field absent for some sampled spans
4) Validate that query engine excludes tombstone buckets by running the raw-timeseries query against storage to confirm data exists but is excluded from live dashboard path
mitigation_actions: Hotfix A (metrics): Add a short-lived in-process buffering layer in metrics-aggregator to hold writes during shard ownership transition; patch avoids writing to tombstone buckets and falls back to previous shard owners for 10s
Hotfix B (tracing): Normalize tenant header keys early in the edge proxy pipeline so the collector always receives 'tenant-id' field; add a fallback mapping rule and a log counter for mismatches
Operator step: Trigger controlled shard rebalance for affected clusters during low traffic windows while deploying hotfixes
Customer-facing: Notify impacted customers with timeline, mitigation steps, and ETA for permanent fix
rollout_plan: 1) Canary deploy metrics hotfix to staffed staging cluster; run ingest-stress & dashboard smoke tests (48h)
2) Canary tracing header normalization in edge proxy on hosted control-plane for 2 mid-size tenants; monitor sampled-span attribution metrics and trace counts (24h)
3) If canaries stable, stage rollouts: Hosted -> Dedicated (staggered per-region) -> Private (provide patch + upgrade notes), each step with 1-hour monitoring window and rollback playbook
4) Post-deploy: run integrity queries to assert no 'tombstone' buckets are used in dashboard queries and sampled-span attribution >99% for affected tenants
qa_criteria: 1) No dashboard tiles report 'no data' for 5-minute windows during 2x baseline ingest in canary
2) Sampled-span counts and per-tenant attribution match pre-incident baselines within 1% during stress test
3) Integration tests added to CI: header-normalization property and metrics-window sovereignty checks
4) Regression tests for shard-owner transitions and tombstone-write prevention are green
